news.title: England 2-3 Spain: World champions win at Wembley in Nations League despite Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane goals
news.lede: Spain showed why they are the best national team in the world by emerging 3-2 winners in a thrilling, chaotic Nations League clash at Wembley, in which England's flaws undermined their exciting attacking play. It was the World Cup final that might have been had England not squandered their advantage against Argentina this summer - but Spain showed the gap in quality in a result which is a major blow to Thomas Tuchel's stated aim of winning this competition. Bad errors from Marc Guehi and Nico O'Reilly helped Lamine Yamal and Alex Baena score Spain's first two and England were cut open through the match, including for Mikel Oyarzabal's winner which came with 16 minutes to play.

news.title: Nations League: Who made an uncharacteristic error? England player ratings v Spain
news.lede: Alex Baena curled in Spain's second goal. England were beaten 3-2 in an entertaining game by world champions Spain in the Nations League - the Three Lions' first match since this summer's World Cup. Lamine Yamal gave Spain the lead before goals from Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane put England ahead. Kane then missed a penalty before Alex Baena curled in to level the score, with Mikel Oyarzabal scoring the winner.

news.title: Ghana to face Angola, Colombia and Iraq at Amputee Football World Cup — MyJoyOnline
news.lede: Ghana’s Black Challenge amputee football national team has been drawn into Group D of the 2026 WAFF World Cup in Mexico, where it will play against Angola, Colombia and Iraq. The draw took place in the Mexican city of San Juan de los Lagos, which will also host the tournament. As MyJoyOnline reports, the Ghanaian team will enter the competition as the reigning African champion and will seek to win its first world title. Ghana’s national team will compete in Group D alongside three opponents from Africa, South America and Asia.

news.title: 2026 Amputee World Cup: Ghana drawn against former champions Angola in Group D
news.lede: Ghana’s national amputee football team, the Black Challenge, have been drawn in Group D of the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup. Ghana’s national amputee football team, the Black Challenge, have been drawn in Group D of the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup alongside former world champions Angola, Colombia and Iraq. The draw sets up an intriguing all-African meeting between Ghana and Angola when the tournament gets underway in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico, in November. Angola remain the only African country to have won the Amputee Football World Cup after lifting the trophy in 2018.

news.title: Arabian Gulf Cup evolve as crucial platform for growth of GCC football
news.lede: MUSCAT: For decades, the Arabian Gulf Cup had evolved far beyond a two-week football tournament. The competition has become an important platform for football development across the region, providing national teams with a valuable testing ground, creating opportunities for players and coaches, strengthening sporting relationships and giving host nations experience in staging major continental and international events. From its early editions, the Gulf Cup has played a significant role in shaping the football landscape of the region. What began as a competition designed to bring Gulf nations together has grown into one of the most followed sporting events in the Arab world, attracting millions of supporters and generating a strong sense of regional identity.

news.title: Bukayo Saka admits World Cup 'scars' remain for England ahead of Nations League
news.lede: The Three Lions look to put the pain of another valiant World Cup semi-final defeat behind them as the Nations League returns. Bukayo Saka seeks to move on from the pain from the summer for England. The Arsenal winger will remember 2026 as the year that he helped his boyhood club claim the Premier League crown for the first time in the Emirates Stadium era. But apart from the regret of losing the Champions League final at the end of May, Three Lions duty also left a lot on the table.
